subject: Greek mythology
prompt: This body of ancient folklore is today usually absorbed into a broader classical designation alongside which other mythology?
why: Greek mythology is the body of myths originally told by the ancient Greeks, today absorbed alongside Roman mythology into the broader designation of classical mythology.

subject: Apollo 11
prompt: The American spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon flew in July of which year?
why: Apollo 11 (July 16-24, 1969) was the American spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon, and the fifth crewed mission of NASA's Apollo program.

subject: Agnosticism
prompt: As a personal attitude this position suspends judgment on the divine, withholding belief — and also withholding what?
why: Agnosticism is a position that questions the existence of God or the divine. On a psychological level it is a personal attitude that suspends judgment, withholding both belief and disbelief.

subject: The World's Billionaires
prompt: This annual ranking lists people estimated to hold a net worth of at least one billion US dollars. Which business magazine compiles it?
why: The World's Billionaires is an annual ranking by the American business magazine Forbes of people who are billionaires, estimated to have a net worth of US$1 billion or more.

subject: States and union territories of India
prompt: India is a federal union of 36 subnational entities: 28 states plus how many union territories?
why: India is a federal union comprising 28 states and 8 union territories, for a total of 36 subnational entities, each subdivided into districts.

subject: Lord's Prayer
prompt: This central Christian prayer attributed to Jesus is known by its Latin incipit as what?
why: The Lord's Prayer, also known by its incipit Our Father (Latin: Pater Noster), is a central Christian prayer attributed to Jesus.

subject: Tsar Bomba
prompt: Code-named Ivan and designated AN602, the most powerful weapon ever constructed and tested was a project of which country?
why: The Tsar Bomba (code name Ivan or Vanya, internal designation AN602) is the most powerful nuclear weapon or weapon of any kind ever constructed and tested. It was a project of the Soviet Union.

subject: Milky Way
prompt: The galaxy containing our Solar System takes its name from how it appears from Earth. What does it look like in the night sky?
why: The Milky Way is the galaxy that includes the Solar System, with the name describing the galaxy's appearance from Earth: a hazy band of light seen in the night sky.

subject: Gaslighting
prompt: This term for manipulating someone into questioning their own perception of reality became popular in the mid-2010s, but derives from a film of which year?
why: Gaslighting is the manipulation of someone into questioning their perception of reality. The term derives from the 1944 film Gaslight and became popular in the mid-2010s.

subject: German language
prompt: A West Germanic language of the Indo-European family, it is spoken mainly in which parts of Europe?
why: German is a West Germanic language in the Indo-European language family, mainly spoken in Western and Central Europe, where it is the majority and official language of several countries.

subject: Jack the Ripper
prompt: This unidentified serial killer was active in 1888 in and around which impoverished London district?
why: Jack the Ripper was an unidentified serial killer active in and around the impoverished Whitechapel district of London, England, in 1888.

subject: Mercury (planet)
prompt: The smallest planet in the Solar System is rocky with only a trace atmosphere, and its surface gravity is slightly higher than which other planet's?
why: Mercury is the first planet from the Sun and the smallest in the Solar System. It is a rocky planet with a trace atmosphere and a surface gravity slightly higher than that of Mars.

subject: Fukushima nuclear accident
prompt: The major nuclear accident that began on 11 March 2011 at the Daiichi plant in Ōkuma had what direct cause?
why: On 11 March 2011 a major nuclear accident started at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant in Ōkuma, Fukushima, Japan. The direct cause was the Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami.

subject: Bhopal disaster
prompt: In December 1984 more than 500,000 people near a pesticide plant in Madhya Pradesh were exposed to which highly toxic gas?
why: On 3 December 1984, over 500,000 people in the vicinity of the Union Carbide India Limited pesticide plant in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, were exposed to the highly toxic gas methyl isocyanate.

subject: Michael (archangel)
prompt: An archangel and warrior of God in three Abrahamic faiths, he also carries a Greek military title meaning brigadier or commander. Which one?
why: Michael, also called Archangel Michael or Michael the Taxiarch, is an archangel and the warrior of God in Judaism, Christianity and Islam, additionally venerated as a saint.
